request.system:
You explain a fitted credit-risk model to a credit risk manager who is not a data scientist. You receive the facts about one model and write a short explanation of what drives its predictions of default.

# The text

- Write 5 to 8 sentences in plain English, most important drivers first.
- Mention an interaction when it matters for the model's predictions.
- Say only what the facts support. Do not round a weak effect up to a strong one, and do not add knowledge about credit risk that the facts do not show.
- When the facts do not settle something, say so ("the data do not settle whether ...") or leave it out.

# The answer

Return one JSON object with one list, `sentences`, each with an `id` (1, 2, 3, ...) and its `text`.
messages:
These are the facts about the model.

Model: an explainable boosting machine (EBM), fitted to predict whether a credit applicant defaults (30,000 applicants). Effects are on the log-odds scale: positive values raise the risk of default. Every band is a 95% band from 100 refits of the model on resampled data.

Features, in the order of their share of the model's importance:
- `PAY_0`: repayment status in September 2005, the latest month (-1 paid in full, 1 to 9 months of payment delay; -2 and 0 are not in the data dictionary, commonly read as no consumption and revolving credit used).
  Share of importance 29.1% (95% band 27.1% to 31.4%); rank 1 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): <= -1: -0.2; 0: -0.5; 1: +0.6; >= 2: +2.3 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +2.45, 95% band [+2.24, +2.61]).
- `LIMIT_BAL`: amount of the given credit in NT dollars, individual and family (supplementary) credit.
  Share of importance 17.0% (95% band 14.8% to 18.0%); rank 2 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): <= 44999: +0.6; 45000-104999: +0.3; 105000-184999: -0.07; 185000-694999: -0.4; >= 695000: -2 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -1.21, 95% band [-1.32, -0.98]).
- `BILL_AMT1`: amount of the bill statement in September 2005, the latest month, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 8.0% (95% band 5.2% to 9.9%); rank 3 to 4 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): <= 10000: -0.17; >= 10001: +0.05 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.74, 95% band [+0.47, +1.02]).
- `PAY_AMT1`: amount paid in September 2005, the latest month, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 7.5% (95% band 6.1% to 9.1%); rank 3 to 4 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): <= 1106: +0.21; 1107-127782: -0.07; >= 127783: -1 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -0.58, 95% band [-0.72, -0.40]).
- `PAY_AMT2`: amount paid in August 2005, the month before, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 4.6% (95% band 2.5% to 6.0%); rank 4 to 7 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): falls by 0.24 (95% band [-0.37, -0.11]) from x = 0 (5th percentile) to x = 19,000 (95th percentile); the shape in between is not resolved at this sample size.
- `AGE`: age in years.
  Share of importance 2.7% (95% band 1.5% to 4.0%); rank 5 to 8 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.02, 95% band [-0.20, +0.15]).
- `BILL_AMT2`: amount of the bill statement in August 2005, the month before, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 2.2% (95% band 1.2% to 4.7%); rank 5 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): rises by 0.31 (95% band [+0.07, +0.54]) from x = 0 (5th percentile) to x = 195,000 (95th percentile); the shape in between is not resolved at this sample size.
- `EDUCATION`: education (1 graduate school, 2 university, 3 high school, 4 others; 0, 5 and 6 are not in the data dictionary).
  Share of importance 0.9% (95% band 0.8% to 2.7%); rank 6 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.04, 95% band [-0.07, +0.18]).
- `PAY_AMT3`: amount paid in July 2005, two months before, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 0.8% (95% band 0.3% to 2.0%); rank 7 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.01, 95% band [-0.11, +0.10]).

Interactions: the model has 5 pairs. The larger ones:
- `PAY_0 & EDUCATION`: share of importance 16.9% (95% band 14.8% to 17.6%).
  Effect of `PAY_0` from -2 to 2: +1.29 (95% band +1.17 to +1.51) when `EDUCATION` = 1, +6.05 (95% band +5.38 to +6.50) when `EDUCATION` = 3.
  Effect of `EDUCATION` from 1 to 3: -0.64 (95% band -0.93 to -0.42) when `PAY_0` = -2, +4.11 (95% band +3.36 to +4.42) when `PAY_0` = 2.
- `BILL_AMT1 & AGE`: share of importance 4.4% (95% band 3.6% to 5.7%).
  Effect of `BILL_AMT1` from 0 to 201,000: +1.55 (95% band +0.71 to +2.12) when `AGE` = 23, -0.07 (95% band -0.38 to +0.46) when `AGE` = 53.
  Effect of `AGE` from 23 to 53: +0.58 (95% band +0.10 to +0.82) when `BILL_AMT1` = 0, -1.04 (95% band -1.48 to -0.27) when `BILL_AMT1` = 201,000.
- `PAY_AMT1 & EDUCATION`: share of importance 2.2% (95% band 1.8% to 3.0%).
  Effect of `PAY_AMT1` from 0 to 18,400: -0.66 (95% band -0.80 to -0.40) when `EDUCATION` = 1, -0.75 (95% band -1.01 to -0.56) when `EDUCATION` = 3.
  Effect of `EDUCATION` from 1 to 3: +0.22 (95% band +0.15 to +0.44) when `PAY_AMT1` = 0, +0.14 (95% band -0.11 to +0.40) when `PAY_AMT1` = 18,400.
- `AGE & BILL_AMT2`: share of importance 2.0% (95% band 0.0% to 2.9%).
  Effect of `AGE` from 23 to 53: -0.21 (95% band -0.47 to +0.15) when `BILL_AMT2` = 0, +0.07 (95% band -0.59 to +0.34) when `BILL_AMT2` = 195,000.
  Effect of `BILL_AMT2` from 0 to 195,000: +0.04 (95% band -0.38 to +0.62) when `AGE` = 23, +0.32 (95% band -0.15 to +0.54) when `AGE` = 53.
- `BILL_AMT1 & EDUCATION`: share of importance 1.7% (95% band 0.0% to 2.6%).
  Effect of `BILL_AMT1` from 0 to 201,000: +0.87 (95% band +0.54 to +1.15) when `EDUCATION` = 1, +0.26 (95% band -0.09 to +0.80) when `EDUCATION` = 3.
  Effect of `EDUCATION` from 1 to 3: +0.39 (95% band +0.04 to +0.59) when `BILL_AMT1` = 0, -0.21 (95% band -0.48 to +0.13) when `BILL_AMT1` = 201,000.

Write the explanation.

content.text: {"sentences":[{"id":1,"text":"The most important driver of predicted default is repayment status in September 2005: applicants who were already one or more months behind on payments carry a clearly higher predicted risk, rising steeply once the delay reaches two months or more, while those who paid in full or were current see a lower risk."},{"id":2,"text":"The second most important driver is the size of the given credit limit: smaller limits are associated with higher predicted default risk and larger limits with lower risk, with the biggest drop at the top end of the range."},{"id":3,"text":"The effect of repayment status depends strongly on education: the jump in predicted risk from being current to being two or more months late is far larger for applicants recorded as high school educated than for those recorded as graduate school educated, so the model separates these groups most sharply on payment history."},{"id":4,"text":"The size of the latest bill and the latest payment matter less: a larger latest bill modestly raises predicted risk, while a larger latest payment lowers it, and the bill effect is stronger for younger applicants, though the data do not settle how the two interact precisely."},{"id":5,"text":"The August payment and bill amounts have small effects that point in the expected directions, falling with larger payments and rising with larger bills, but the shape of these effects between the lower and upper ends of the range cannot be resolved at this sample size."},{"id":6,"text":"Age, education on its own, and the July payment have effects that are too small to distinguish from zero, so the model does not rely on them in a way the data can confirm."}]}
